scale.source: CLDR RBNF uk renders 10^9 as "один мільярд" and 10^12 as "один більйон": Ukrainian names 10^9 "мільярд" and 10^12 "більйон", so a -illion counts in the short scale. Wiktionary (en), "трильйон": "trillion".

group_mark.source: CLDR common/main/uk.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the group symbol is U+00A0, a no-break space. No dot groups digits.

decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/uk.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the decimal symbol is a comma.

space_groups.source: CLDR common/main/uk.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the group symbol is a no-break space, so groups of three digits after a space are one number.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR RBNF uk writes a plural scale word only after its count ("дві тисячі", 2000). A plural scale word with no count names an amount, not a number. Wiktionary (en), "сотня": "сотні тисяч людей", "hundreds of thousands of people".

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF uk %spellout-cardinal-masculine renders 10^6, 2 x 10^6, 5 x 10^6 and 21 x 10^6 as "один мільйон", "два мільйони", "пʼять мільйонів", "двадцять один мільйон": the scale noun takes the number and case its count governs. The count governs by its last word, so the singular also follows 21. The scale words of this lexicon are scale_numeral entries whose plural flag carries that agreement.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF uk: "20: двадцять[ >>];", no conjunction between tens and units.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF uk: "100: сто[ >>];", no conjunction after the hundreds.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF uk renders 1001 as "одна тисяча один", no conjunction between groups.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF uk renders 1100 as "одна тисяча сто" and 1500 as "одна тисяча пʼятсот": no joiner stands before a round hundred after the thousands.

hundred_counts_below_thousand.source: unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 (CLDR RBNF uk data), %spellout-cardinal, rendering of 2100: "дві тисячі сто": the hundred after the thousands is the next group, so a hundred multiplier takes no count of a thousand or more.

compound_parts_by_role.source: compound_words is true, with the source quoted there: the compound number words it cites join cardinal and ordinal words and joiners only, so a fraction noun or a collective is no part of one ("petin|dvajset" is no split).

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR RBNF uk writes no comma between two classes (1001, 1100 and 1500 in the joiner settings above). No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR RBNF uk renders 1001 as "одна тисяча один": no conjunction stands before the last group.

ordinal_style.source: CLDR RBNF uk renders 2023 in %spellout-ordinal-masculine as "дві тисячі двадцять третій": only the last word is ordinal.

compound_words.source: CLDR RBNF uk writes 2000th as one word ("двотисячний"). Український правопис (2019), § 38 "Складні числівники", writes such ordinals with digits and a hyphen ("3-ти́сячний"). A word that is a sequence of number words reads as its parts.

bare_noun_counts_one.source: Ukrainian has no article, so a singular collective or fraction noun alone counts one. Wiktionary (en), "чверть": "чверть години", "a quarter of an hour".

decimal_fractions.source: CLDR RBNF uk renders 2.5 as "дві цілих пʼять десятих": the decimals are a fraction whose denominator is a power of ten.

ordinal_form_part_takes_no_digits.source: Maintainer ruling on numtag issue 98 for ru, uk and pl, after Д. Э. Розенталь, "Справочник по правописанию и литературной правке", 4th edition (1985), § 45, item 3: "Дробные числительные пишутся раздельно, например: две пятых (2/5)". A fraction in digits is written with a slash, so digits before a part word that is also a plural ordinal form count things: "3 пятых класса" is three fifth-grade classes. The uk plural part word is the plural ordinal form too ("п'ятих").

joiner.source: Wiktionary (en), "половина" and "пів" give the half; "з" (also "із") joins a half to a whole: a paraphrase, the usage example is not on those pages.

decimal_marker.source: CLDR RBNF uk: "x.x: << $(cardinal,one{ціла}other{цілих})$ >%%fractions-feminine>;" and the genitive "цілої".

minus_idioms.source: This lexicon lists no Ukrainian idiom that puts "мінус" before a positive number.

number_name.source: СУМ (Словник української мови, 1970-1980), "один": "Один і той же; Один і той самий - такий самий, той самий; однаковий. Зурна повторяла один і той самий голос" (Коцюб.); "Одне (одно) і те ж; Одне (одно) і (й) те саме - те саме; однакове. Влада і народ у нас - одне і те ж" (Козл.). СУМ, "той" 8: "у сполученнях той же, той [же] самий, та (те) ж, та [ж] сама, те [ж] саме". The set phrase means "the same" and counts nothing. The list holds its case forms in each gender and the plural, with "і" or "й" and with "самий" or "же" or "ж".

article_one.source: Ukrainian has no article; "один" is a numeral.

of.source: Ukrainian marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

fraction_of.source: Ukrainian marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

denominator_particle.source: Ukrainian has no particle like Portuguese "avos".

class_noun.source: Ukrainian names no digit class with a singular noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: Wiktionary (en), "пів": "пів року", "half a year": the half is its own word, read by the half role.

abbreviation.source: No Ukrainian number word in this lexicon is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/uk.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae): the decimal symbol is a comma; a comma before the first digit marks decimals.

word_apostrophe.source: Український правопис (2019), § 7 "Апостроф": "Апостроф пишемо перед" я, ю, є, ї after a labial consonant, as in "б’ю, п’ять, п’є". The page writes U+2019, CLDR writes U+02BC, and texts also use U+0027: all three are the same letter.

ordinal_suffix_mark.source: CLDR RBNF uk %digits-ordinal-masculine: "0: =#,##0=-$(ordinal,few{ій}other{ий})$;": the ordinal ending follows the digits after a hyphen.

range_cue.source: Wiktionary (en), "між": "between, among", expressing position in space or time.
